subject: Off-network deployment feasibility & roadmap questions
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ellen Park <ellen.park@acme-payments.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@cloudops.co>
Date: Mon, 11 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Off-network deployment feasibility & roadmap questions

Team — looping you all together after the Acme kickoff. They want an "off-network" deployment (VPC-like with optional on-prem agents) and have a short pilot window. High-level asks from Acme: KMS integration with customer HSM, no external egress for model artifacts, audit logs retained for 7 years, and deterministic failover behavior. I attached the RFP extract and their requirements spreadsheet.

Hi Ellen / Sanjay — we’ll run through feasibility internally and come back with a short decision brief and proposed minimal pilot scope. To get alignment, I need the following from each function by EOD Wednesday:
- Monica: initial ops checklist for packaging runtime and bootstrap (networking pre-reqs, required ports, images).
- Marcus: rough SRE staffing delta (on-call, deployment runbook, emergency rollback).
- Grace: commercial constraints we should surface (support SLAs, pricing implications for isolated capacity).

Quick notes/constraints from product:
- We can support customer-managed KMS via our KMS proxy but HSM integration will need a security review and likely a limited Engineering spike.
- Air-gapped artifact delivery is possible but will require signed, hermetic bundles and a delivery SOP with Ops.

Please reply inline with gaps/estimations. I’ll consolidate into a one-page decision brief for Execs and Acme.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Product, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Off-network deployment feasibility & roadmap questions

Karthik — drafted a preliminary ops checklist and flagged three high-risk items (see inline). Short summary:

1) Packaging & delivery
- We can create signed tarball artifacts and SHA256 manifests. Air-gap delivery requires a secure endpoint on Acme side and a validation hook in bootstrap. Estimate: 2 engineer-weeks to produce a hardened packaging pipeline and validation tooling.

2) Network pre-reqs
- Minimum: outbound to our telemetry endpoint (optional for air-gap, but requires local telemetry ingestion). If Acme insists on zero egress, we need to run local telemetry collectors and an offline log ingestion path. Estimate: 1 engineer-week for local collector work.

3) Secrets/KMS
- We support wrapping keys with customer KMS; HSM-specific operations (PKCS#11) are not currently supported in our runtime. Integrating PKCS#11 for direct HSM calls is a non-trivial security spike: 3-4 engineer-weeks + security review.

Attachments: brief ops-checklist (pasted below) and a short matrix of what we must own vs what Acme must provide. Happy to present this on Thursday.

-- Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.ai

Thanks Monica — appreciate the breakdown. Operationally, here's what SRE needs to make this low-risk for our platform:

- On-call overhead: pilot will require 1 dedicated on-call engineer for first 4 weeks (rotation possible after stabilization). This is due to support surface (airgapped delivery + customer-side infra).
- Runbook and rollback: need a canned rollback (switch traffic to hosted fallback model) and an emergency key-rot path if customer-managed KMS fails.
- CI/CD: we'll need a staging harness that emulates the customer's restricted network. Estimate: 2 SRE-weeks to build the harness and 1 SRE-week to author runbooks and playbooks.
- Observability: if full zero-egress is required, we'll need to support local log retention and secure periodic exports. Adds 1 engineer-week.

Total rough SRE delta for pilot: 4-5 engineer-weeks + 1 FTE for the first month of the pilot (on-call). If Acme covers part of the on-call (embedded model), that reduces our burden.

Question for Grace: do we treat the pilot as a paid engagement (professional services) or as a pre-sales proof-of-concept? That determines staffing and SLA expectations.

— Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Engineering Manager
marcus@redwood.ai

All — quick commercial read: for a pilot with the constraints described, legal and finance will expect a paid Professional Services engagement (covers dev work, security review, and a named SRE on-call). Pricing guidance: recommend booking 6-8 PS weeks + a reserved capacity uplift (we price isolated deployments at a 35% premium over hosted unit cost due to ops friction).

If leadership wants a strategic approach (we absorb some PS cost), we should limit scope to: a single non-production datacenter, customer-managed KMS via wrapping (no direct HSM integration), and a timeboxed SLA with clear fallbacks to hosted. That reduces the engineering delta significantly.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) Karthik compiles decision brief with two paths: "Paid Pilot" and "Constrained Strategic Pilot".
2) Marcus & Monica provide concise engineering BANDWIDTH estimate (in FTE-weeks).
3) Grace to draft a simple PS statement-of-work template for approval.

Ellen — do you have flexibility to accept KMS-wrapping (not direct HSM calls) for an initial pilot? If not, tell us and we’ll flag HSM as a separate, longer-term project.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.ai
